# Feature: Author Guidance for Report Templates

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-005
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)
**Extends**: FEAT-FP-004 (`.spec-lite/features/feature_report_templates.md`)

FEAT-FP-004 shipped report templates: an author writes Markdown with `{{ slot }}`
placeholders, Yantra generates a TypeBox schema from the parsed manifest, the
model fills slots, and the **runtime renders the document** so structural
deviation is unrepresentable.

What a template cannot express today is **intent**. `{{ summary | markdown,
max_words=200 }}` tells the model how long the section is, never what it should
say. The author's only levers are the slot key and the enclosing heading, so
_"lead with the revenue number, then the driver, name the segment not the region"_
has nowhere to live.

This feature adds **optional prose guidance** — attached to individual slots and,
once, to the whole document. Guidance is advisory instruction for the model only.
It **must never appear in the rendered report**.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules are in `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides here.

### Approach

**What the author writes:**

```markdown
---
name: exec-brief
description: Weekly executive brief
guidance: British English. CFO audience. Never speculate beyond the sources.
tags: [work, weekly]
---

# {{ title | text }}

## Executive Summary

<!-- guidance:
Lead with the headline revenue number, then explain the driver
in one sentence. Name the segment, not the region.
-->

{{ summary | markdown, max_words=200 }}
```

- `<!-- guidance: … -->` occupies its own line(s) and binds to the **next**
  placeholder in the body, surviving intervening blank lines and headings.
- Frontmatter `guidance:` is the document-level note. It sits beside `description`
  and has zero interaction with the positional rule.
- Vocabulary is `guidance` everywhere — marker, manifest field, CLI column — per
  the CLI-consistency rule in memory.

**The delivery channel already exists.** `slotDescription()` in
`packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/template-params.ts` is the single place
per-slot semantics reach the model; kind, columns, and constraints all render
through it. Guidance joins that string, and document-level guidance appends to the
enclosing `report` object's description. Tool schemas persist across turns, so
**no prompt text changes anywhere** — `promptAddendumFor` and
`buildTemplateCompletionNudge` stay untouched.

**The architectural decision: strip at parse time, not render time.**
`parseTemplate` removes guidance directive lines from the body it stores in the
manifest and computes slot `offset` values against that **stripped** body. This
makes leaking structurally impossible rather than render-time-conditional, and
`renderTemplate` needs **no change** — it splices into the same body it was
handed. It mirrors FEAT-FP-004's founding principle: don't validate against a bad
outcome, make it unrepresentable.

The mechanic is two independent counters in the one existing pass over
`parse.ts:89-136`:

```ts
const rawBody = frontmatter.value.body;
const parts: string[] = []; // kept lines, verbatim, terminators included
let bodyOffset = 0; // running start offset into the STRIPPED body
let open: { text: string[]; line: number } | null = null;
let pending: { text: string; line: number } | null = null;

for (const line of sourceLines(rawBody)) {
  const lineNumber = frontmatter.value.bodyStartLine + line.index; // UNCHANGED
  // guidance classification → on a directive line: `continue`
  //   (parts not appended, bodyOffset not advanced)

  parts.push(rawBody.slice(line.start, line.end)); // includes \r\n
  // heading detection: byte-for-byte unchanged
  for (const match of line.content.matchAll(placeholder)) {
    const bound = pending;
    pending = null; // first placeholder wins
    slots.push({ ...parsed.value, guidance: bound?.text ?? null, offset: bodyOffset + index });
  }
  // maskRanges malformed-brace checks: unchanged
  bodyOffset += line.end - line.start;
}
```

Invariant: `bodyOffset` at the top of a kept line equals that line's start in
`parts.join('')`, because `parts` receives exactly `line.end - line.start`
characters for every line that advances the counter. `lineNumber` still derives
from `line.index` over the **raw** body, so parse errors keep reporting
complete-file line numbers (locked by `parse.spec.ts:120-124`). One pass, no
offset remapping.

`hash` continues to cover the complete raw text — a guidance edit _is_ a template
revision and must produce a new provenance hash.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **`guidance` is a sibling of `constraints`, never inside it.**
  `TemplateSlotConstraints` is `.strict()` and numeric-only, and
  `formatConstraints` would render `guidance=Lead with the…` into the CONSTRAINTS
  column.

- **Guidance is advisory; `validateSlots` is not changed.** Authors who want
  enforcement use the existing numeric constraints. Do not over-promise this.

- **Reject `{{` and `}}` inside guidance text at parse time.** `validateSlots`
  rejects any slot value matching `/\{\{.*?\}\}/s` as _"must not echo template
  placeholder syntax."_ Guidance reading _"do not put `{{ risks }}` here"_ would be
  injected into the schema description, invite the echo, and trigger an
  undiagnosable `REPORT_INVALID` retry loop. Stripping directives before the
  placeholder scan means `maskRanges` never sees those braces, so nothing else
  catches it.

- **Trust class.** Heading text already reaches the model unsanitized through
  `slotDescription`; guidance is the same class (a local author-owned file).
  TASK-003 also adds the ANSI strip to `staticHeading`, so the trust story is not
  "we sanitize the new author string but not the old one."

- **Fenced code blocks are not special-cased.** The parser has no fence awareness
  today — headings and `{{ }}` inside ``` fences are already treated as real. A
  directive inside a fence is stripped too. Adding fence tracking for guidance
  alone would be inconsistent; adding it everywhere would silently change what
  counts as a slot in existing templates. Document the behavior instead.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Mapping string `minChars`/`maxChars` to JSON Schema `minLength`/`maxLength`.
  Tempting (it would move errors to provider-time, FEAT-FP-004's stated principle)
  but `minLength` counts UTF-16 units while `validateString` counts code points, so
  they disagree on astral characters and the provider would reject payloads the
  runtime accepts. Recorded in TODO as a decision, not an oversight.
- Guidance that varies by run (params, dates, captured values). Guidance is static
  template text.
- Any change to `promptAddendumFor`, `buildTemplateCompletionNudge`, or
  `validateSlots`.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

Two nullable string fields on existing protocol schemas in
`packages/protocol/src/schemas/report-template.ts`. No storage-layer change —
templates remain single self-describing `.md` files under `templatesRoot()`.

### Entities & Attributes

- **TemplateSlot** (extended)
  - `guidance` (string | null) — author guidance appended to this slot's
    model-facing description. Required-nullable, `.min(1)`, matching the
    `name`/`description`/`columns` convention. Placed between `constraints` and
    `offset`.

- **TemplateManifest** (extended)
  - `guidance` (string | null) — document-level author guidance. Required-nullable,
    `.min(1)`. Placed after `description`.

- **ReportTemplate** (on-disk, unchanged shape) gains an optional frontmatter
  `guidance:` key and zero or more `<!-- guidance: … -->` body directives.

### Relationships

- TemplateManifest 1:N TemplateSlot — each slot carries at most one guidance
  string, bound positionally at parse time.
- No change to `TemplatedReport`: `template.hash` already pins the revision that
  produced a document, so guidance needs no separate record.

### Indexes & Constraints

- Per-slot guidance cap: **500 code points** after whitespace normalization. The
  tool schema is re-sent every turn — a 20-slot template at 500 each is roughly
  2.5K tokens of permanent per-turn overhead.
- Document-level cap: **1000 code points**. Charged once, so it gets the larger
  budget for a real style guide.
- Guidance may not contain `{{` or `}}`, nor raw ANSI escape bytes
  (`\u001b` / `\u009b`).
- Guidance may not bind to the reserved `sources` slot — that slot is excluded from
  the generated schema, so binding there would silently discard the author's text.
- No `.max()` in the Zod schema. The manifest is never deserialized from disk or
  network (`document.json` stores only a `ReportTemplateReference`; the sole
  `safeParse` call site is `parse.ts:155`), so the parser is the single enforcement
  point and a duplicated limit would drift.

> **Failure-mode note while debugging:** `TemplateSlot`'s inner object is **not**
> `.strict()`, so an undeclared `guidance` key is **silently stripped** — skipping
> the protocol change makes the feature a no-op with green tests elsewhere.
> `TemplateManifest` **is** `.strict()`, so it fails loudly as `Unrecognized key(s)`
> mapped to line 1.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. Guidance adds no credential surface and no new I/O — templates are
  already local author-owned files read through the existing store.

- **Error Handling**: Every guidance failure is a **parse error** returned through
  the existing `Result<TemplateManifest, TemplateParseError[]>` channel with a
  one-based complete-file line number — never a throw, and never a runtime failure.
  This means a malformed directive is caught by `yantra template lint` and by the
  `--template` resolution path _before_ a run directory is created (exit 1,
  validation), consistent with FEAT-FP-004. Errors accumulate: one pass collects
  every problem in the file rather than stopping at the first. `validateSlots` and
  the `REPORT_INVALID` retry loop are untouched — guidance can never cause an
  in-flight publish failure.

- **Logging**: Unchanged, and deliberately so. Guidance is user-authored prose and
  is **never logged**, exactly like the template body. The run manifest continues to
  record `template: { name, hash, source }`; because `hash` covers the complete raw
  text, a guidance edit produces a new hash, so an audit can still tell precisely
  which template revision produced a given `document.*`.

- **Security**: Guidance is the same trust class as template heading text, which
  already reaches the model unsanitized through `slotDescription`. TASK-003 closes
  that asymmetry by adding the ANSI strip to `staticHeading` as well. The `{{`/`}}`
  rejection prevents an author from accidentally arming the `validateSlots`
  placeholder-echo check against their own run. Guidance never reaches
  `document.md` or `document.html`, so it cannot contribute to the inert-HTML
  surface; note that `escapeHtml` would render a leaked comment as _visible_
  `&lt;!-- … --&gt;` text, which is precisely why strip-at-parse is the right
  architecture rather than a render-time filter.
